solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To throw groom into tailored suit doable?

indicators.note: into says the grooming word is placed inside the rearranged letters
a suit that is tailored is cut and reshaped, so the letters of suit and doable are rearranged

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a groom can be squeezed into a made-to-measure wedding suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To throw' is the definition, a verb; 'tailored' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container signal, so the groom goes inside the reshuffled suit doable.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert or confuse someone is to throw them, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Popular summer flower opening

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion
a summer month: August, abbreviated Aug
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ural is a Russian river

explanation.surface: A well-loved summer bloom is just coming into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword river (something that flows), and 'summer' is a summer month, AUG for August.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the first, opening one, as with an inaugural speech or match.

clue.text: Wood, broadcaster on the radio?

indicators.note: words heard on the radio are spoken, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: one who broadcasts scatters seed by hand: a seeder

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a radio presenter being wooden.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting originally meant sowing seed by scattering it widely, so the broadcaster here is a sower, not a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant timber from a coniferous tree, a type of wood.

clue.text: Heading for mountain, the gear changes variable for many cycles

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken from mountain
the gear changes, so the letters of the and gear are rearranged

parts.note: in algebra a variable is often written as x, y or z

explanation.surface: A cyclist heading for the hills shifts gear, varying pace over many turns of the pedals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges 'the gear' into the middle stretch; Z, the algebraic variable, closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a million cycles per second, so many cycles in each second.

clue.text: Fruit cut for ape

indicators.note: cut means a fruit name loses its final letter

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone slices fruit to feed a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter, E, of ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for orang-utan, the great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Experienced runner after run, wiping brow

indicators.note: after puts the river behind the shortened word
wiping the brow removes the top, the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter
a river runs, so a runner is a river; the Derwent is an English river

explanation.surface: An athlete, wiping their forehead after a run, has been through the mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river, the Derwent, which flows through Cumbria and Derbyshire in England; 'wiping brow' strips R from RUN to leave UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undergone something is to have experienced or gone through it.

clue.text: Love an access to opportunity, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals a spoken likeness, a word sounding the same

parts.note: opportunity proverbially opens a door, so access to it is a door

explanation.surface: A wistful question whether love opens doors to opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: In British, non-rhotic speech the phrase 'a door' sounds the same as the word meaning to love deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply, a plain synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: European victory on key horse

parts.note: V is short for victory, as in V-sign
Enter is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A European wins with a key horse in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the three-day equestrian competition.

clue.text: Winning, opportunity to get result

parts.note: a team ahead is said to be up
a shot is a chance or attempt at something

explanation.surface: Someone in the lead takes a chance to secure the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or consequence of something is its upshot.

clue.text: Crisscross weave positioned on middle of lapel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
middle of picks the central letter of the five-letter word lapel

parts.note: positioned means laid, placed down

explanation.surface: A tartan pattern sewn onto the centre of a jacket lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts LAID after P, the middle letter of LAPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is tartan cloth, woven in a pattern of crossing coloured stripes.

clue.text: Overly elaborate raids gone awry

indicators.note: things gone awry are twisted out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper verdict on botched raids that were too ambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' is fodder, not part of the indicator: 'awry' reshuffles RAIDS GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means pompous and over-ambitious, more impressive in intent than effect.

clue.text: English painter — don't share his work with Holbein for a start

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to oneself
a painter's work is art

indicators.note: for a start takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A painter is told not to share his work with Holbein.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans Holbein the Younger was court painter to Henry VIII; he only supplies an H.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an eighteenth-century English painter and satirical engraver.

clue.text: Possibly Top Gun getting screened by bloke

indicators.note: screened by means hidden behind or surrounded by the other word

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is a man or bloke
a firearm is an arm

explanation.surface: Someone shows the film Top Gun to a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gun is the film, but 'Top' is the definition and 'Gun' a separate piece; 'Possibly' marks a top as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is an example of an item of clothing, such as a shirt or blouse.

clue.text: Worn out — like the wheel on an American car?

definitions.text: like the wheel on an American car?
definitions.meaning: American spelling writes tyre as tire, so a wheel fitted with one is fitted with a tire

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: US spelling 'tire' for the rubber ring makes a wheel wearing one tire-d.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn out is weary, and a wheel fitted with an American tire is jokily 'tire-d'.

clue.text: Stop people getting punishment

parts.note: to dam a flow is to stop it
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A demand to stop people from being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is eternal punishment in hell, condemnation for sin.

clue.text: Big noise always a criminal

parts.note: a racket is a loud din
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A loud, ever-present troublemaker is labelled a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic short form of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal running a fraudulent or extortionate business.

clue.text: Siren defining danger, ultimately, in fried food

indicators.note: defining is read as de-fining, setting bounds around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a siren is a seductive woman, a flirt or coquette

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A temptress spells out the danger of deep-fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' works as 'enclosing': COQUETTE surrounds R, the last letter of 'danger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small cake of minced food coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

clue.text: Broadcast tie with radio link initially as commentary

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of tie and radio are dispersed and reassembled
initially takes the first letter of link

explanation.surface: A radio link is set up to broadcast a match commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' scrambles TIE RADIO into EDITORIA, then L from 'link'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper leader is the paper's opinion piece, its commentary on events.

clue.text: Ending in nick, a beastly prison for priests, say, that's in Michigan

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests; say marks them as an example
a zoo jokingly imprisons beasts

explanation.surface: A tale of a prison for priests turned into a zoo, somewhere in Michigan.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a zoo for Tibetan priests, as if they were the South American animals spelt with a double L.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in south-west Michigan, a place that fits the description.

clue.text: Asian city, Asian capital lacking an eastern energy

indicators.note: lacking says the word an is dropped from the capital

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, in Asia Minor
chi (qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A city compared with an Asian capital short of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian capital' is not the definition: it is ANKARA, losing its opening AN to leave KARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan, on the Arabian Sea coast of South Asia.

clue.text: One piercing classical chord

indicators.note: one piece piercing another goes inside it

parts.note: trad, short for traditional, means classical in style
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single note cuts through a classical chord.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a chord of three notes, root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Slimmer German chap?

definitions.meaning: a person on a diet trying to lose weight
A common German male first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slimmer' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun, one who slims.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a diet is a slimmer, and the same spelling is a German man's name.

clue.text: Daily struggle to carry in organ backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the assembled letters are read right to left
in places the carrying word inside the organ

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
to cart something is to carry it

explanation.surface: A daily grind of hauling a church organ around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the carrying word inside the organ to give ECARTAR, and 'backwards' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the relentless competitive grind of working life.

clue.text: First degree as a fillip

definitions.meaning: the first note, or degree, of a musical scale, its keynote

explanation.walkthrough: 'First degree' suggests a university qualification or a murder charge; it is the first degree of a musical scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The keynote of a scale is its first degree, and a pick-me-up or boost is a fillip.

clue.text: Resin in time, leaking from below

indicators.note: from below says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Resin seeps out of a tree over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden word no indicator; 'in' is that indicator. In a down clue 'from below' reads IMELE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and incense.

clue.text: Free melody not beginning to inspire ladies and gents

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the shortened melody takes the toilets inside it
not beginning means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a tune is a melody
in Britain the Ladies and the Gents are public toilets, loos

explanation.surface: A free melody that fails to inspire, played in public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' drops T from TUNE to leave UNE; 'to inspire' breathes LOOS into it. Ladies and Gents are British signs for public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set free, to release from bonds.

clue.text: Theme ending in travel book

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its final letter

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: The theme that closes out a travel book.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemma is the heading or subject of a composition or annotation, its theme.

clue.text: Comfortable housing in Europe, say?

indicators.note: housing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: content means comfortable, at ease

explanation.surface: Someone happily settled into a home in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Europe as one example of the landmass type.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is an example of one of the world's great landmasses.

clue.text: Yellow puzzle for The Listener

indicators.note: for a listener means as heard, so a word sounding alike is wanted

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths

explanation.surface: A yellow-themed puzzle set for the Listener, a famously hard crossword series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a celebrated, notoriously difficult crossword in The Times; here it just means someone hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is a pale yellow colour, named after the corn.

clue.text: Distortion of "second", Liberian minute

indicators.note: a distortion twists the shape, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minute and a second get twisted by a Liberian clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' and 'minute' look like time units; 'minute' is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute (my-NEWT) means tiny, too small to matter.
